text:
48. Some respondents wondered whether the inclusion of a mitigating factor a bout
employment was discriminatory, and was likely to operate against those of a lower
socio-economic status, who are less likely to be in employment, perhaps through
no fault of their own. This might in turn lead to members of this group being
sentenced more harshly, thus increasing any marginalisation.
Page | 12
The Sentencing Process Guideline
Scottish Sentencing Council report on public consultation exercise

49. The Council reflected carefully on this point, and ultimately was minded to remove
this factor from the guideline . In doing so, however, it reaffirmed that in general
these lists are not intended to be exhaustive; and that there may well be cases in
which the employment status of the offender, or for that matter their willingness to
pursue training or educational opportunities, form part of the whole circumstances
of a sentencing decision and are quite properly taken into account in reaching that
decision.
What does the Council intend to do?
